question: The shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object is called ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the **shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object**, measured along a straight line. It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. 
 
• The **magnitude** of displacement represents the shortest path covered, while its direction indicates the direction of motion from the initial to the final position. 
 
• Displacement can be **positive, negative, or zero**. For example: 
 
 
• If an object moves from point A to point B in a straight line, its displacement is positive in the direction of motion. 
 
• If it moves back to its starting point, the displacement becomes zero. 
 
• Displacement can also be negative if the direction of motion is opposite to the defined positive direction. 
 
 
 
• Displacement is **independent of the path taken**. Even if the object moves along a curved or zigzag path, the displacement only considers the straight-line distance between the starting and ending points.
